At its September 13th, 2021 meeting, PDCS provided direction that in advance of a concept plan,
a recommendation for swell boundaries in the University Heights, Neighborhood 3, or UH-3, the Broad forward for endorsement.

This is a unique direction, as specific land use boundaries are not typically determined until a full concept plan is brought forward to allow for the various studies required for a concept plan to be completed.
But this isn't necessarily surprising, given the unique nature and value of the small swell and northeastern swell and the interests they have generated in the community.
Historically, the City has done substantial work to proactively identify boundaries for the northeast and small swells,
ahead of development occurring in the area. This started back in nearly 2000s with the first iteration of the northeast swell development guidelines,
followed by an earlier iteration of the University Heights sector plan, both of which were updated in 2012 and 2013 respectively.
In 2017, Council then directed administration to bring together a group to address issues arising from development adjacent to the northeast swell.
This group called the northeast swell working group consisted of representatives of New Boston City Council, the Swail Watchers City Administration,
another local topic experts has needed.
Knowing there was questions if we had the right data to determine swell boundaries, we took the opportunity to involve the swell working group
in determining the scope of the natural area screening or NES for the area that was completed by Saskatoon Land as part of the UH3 concept plan process.
Two meetings were held in 2018 first to determine what information was missing and second to discuss the process with Saskatoon Land.
As a result, City Administration worked with Saskatoon Land to confirm the scope of the NES before it was released based on input from the swell working group.

The results in environmental, dynamic ink or EDI being selected to complete the NES, they worked on this through 2018 or 2019 and 2020 and ended up providing this map as a recommendation for swell boundaries.
Prior to the NES being completed, City Administration reviewed the document numerous times to confirm it met the scope of the project as well as any applicable policies, bylaws and standards.
In addition to this review, the NES was released publicly and comments on it received from me Watson, the Swail Watchers C-Pause, Saskatoon and nature society and wild about Saskatoon.
City Administration completed a thorough review of these comments and discussion of various options for swell boundaries occurred at a swell working group on December 7th, 2021.
The hope was to gain consensus on swell boundaries and bring forward this bringing this forward for council's endorsement.
Unfortunately, no consensus was achieved resulting in three options being brought forward for council's consideration.
Each of these options is seen as viable options.
The first of these are the boundaries recommended in the NES. This option provides additional buffering and protection of the ecological sensitive areas within both the swells,
while allowing for less ecological valuable and disturb areas to be considered for stormwater management infrastructure or municipal reserve.
The second option is based on administration's analysis of the UH-3 NES and all stakeholder comments received.

This option expands beyond the NES recommendations to incorporate additional native grassline habitat within the swells, while also providing additional buffers for the small swell and the riddle tailing to a logical site.
Areas recommended for the swell, boundary expansion, and buffers tend to be in places where either slopes or wetlands would access pinch points for wildlife movement.
These recommendations reflect comments received from Mewawson and others based on their observations and experience doing natural area management work both in and around the swells.
The third option expands on option 2 and is based on a detailed review of the UH-3 NES overlaid with Mewawson's experience studying the swells throughout their work.

This option incorporates additional native grassline area into the northeastern swell while also allowing greater wildlife movement between the areas of the swell and providing additional buffering of the lack.
This is the option that PDCS is recommending for council's endorsement.
So effectively this wraps up my presentation.

The endorsed boundaries would then guide the developer and preparing their concept plan and guided administration in the review of that concept plan once it is submitted.
Through the concept plan process there will be additional opportunity for public discussion and review of what is being proposed.
Formal final boundaries for the swell will be confirmed via the concept plan approval.
